terminal_record.title: Trump Pardons Hedge-Fund Manager Drew “Bo” Brownstein
terminal_record.description_short: Trump granted Drew “Bo” Brownstein a full pardon in January 2021 after his securities-fraud conviction.
terminal_record.description_medium: On January 20, 2021, the White House announced that President Donald Trump had granted Drew “Bo” Brownstein a full pardon. DOJ’s index lists his securities-fraud conviction and a sentence of one year and one day in prison, three years of supervised release, and a $7,500 fine. The Colorado Sun reported that Brownstein ran a Denver hedge fund and pleaded guilty to illegal stock trading. The sources do not establish that donations influenced the pardon.
terminal_record.description_long: On January 20, 2021, the archived White House press secretary’s statement announced a full pardon for Drew Brownstein and said he had been convicted of insider trading and had paid his fines and forfeitures. The Justice Department’s pardon index lists Drew Kallman Brownstein under its January 19, 2021 grants. It identifies the Southern District of New York case as securities fraud and records a sentence of one year and one day in prison, three years of supervised release, and a $7,500 fine. The Colorado Sun reported that Brownstein ran a Denver hedge fund, pleaded guilty in 2011 to illegal stock trading, and was pardoned as Trump prepared to leave office. These sources establish the clemency event and Brownstein’s conviction. They do not establish the frozen description’s claim that associates donated to Trump-affiliated PACs, that contributions affected the decision, or that clemency was exchanged for donations. Those claims and the Government Corruption framing are removed from this narrowed proposal; no causal or donor relationship is asserted.
